Siauliai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Siauliai's Jewish community, established in 1701, grew into a major industrial force after 1855 — Haim Frenkel's small hide-dressing plant became one of the largest in Russia within just a few years. By Lithuanian independence, Siauliai was the country's second-largest city with its second-largest Jewish community, which elected its own deputy mayor and supported 15 synagogues and a yeshiva. The city was the birthplace of Viktor Brenner (1871–1920s), the sculptor and engraver famous for designing the United States Lincoln cent, and of Dov Shilanski (1924–2010), an Israeli politician who served as Speaker of the Knesset. About 10,000 of Siauliai's Jews were shot in nearby forests within the first weeks of Nazi occupation; survivors were confined to two ghettos, and several thousand more were deported to the Stutthof concentration camp after the ghettos' liquidation in July 1944 — no more than 500 of Siauliai's prewar Jews survived the war. This cemetery, founded around 1749 and enclosed by a distinctive two-meter stone wall, survived the Nazi occupation itself, only to be razed by bulldozers during the Soviet era; a handful of surviving local Jews were forced to move their loved ones' remains to the city's public cemetery, which now has three sections for Jews.
